title: Personalization Increases Affective Alignment but Has Role-Dependent Effects on Epistemic Independence in LLMs

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing LLM responses generated from generic prompts versus personalized prompts (which include randomly sampled user demographic and personality traits) across various tasks like personal advice, moral judgments, and debates. The methodology measures changes in affective alignment (emotional validation, hedging) and epistemic alignment (framing acceptance, positional stability, and flip rate in multi-turn interactions) using an LLM-as-a-judge.
